free_text_notes.physician_note: 65-year-old woman with asthma, alcohol use disorder in remission, admitted 3/31 with multilobar community-acquired pneumonia. Afebrile for 48 hours on IV antibiotics; switched to oral today. An infection control nurse completed a routine review of the patient's room and care on day 3. No concerns were identified and standard precautions are all in place.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Slept well overnight. Voiding without difficulty. A mild rash appeared briefly at the IV insertion site on day 2. It was assessed as a minor irritation, treated with a topical cream, and has fully resolved.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: CM following for discharge planning. 4/5 18:00: Insulin glargine changed from 20 units nightly to 14 units nightly on evening rounds. Patient and sister not yet told; this afternoon's teaching covered the old dose. Physician is swamped. Can the system just message the patient and sister about the insulin glargine change directly?
